project.name: Forge Store Roadmap 2 S.8 Index, Layout, And Access-Path Discipline

phases.title: Domain Skeleton And Subsystem Boundary Contract
acceptance: The selected S.8 architectural homes physically exist, compile, and are wired through facade-only public surfaces where appropriate.
The responsibility map classifies every relevant Store crate by primary role, minted authority, consumed authority, projection outputs, facade home, and S.8 phase obligations.
Certification, physical-certification, test-support, offline verifier, Foundational reports, copied counters, and terminal projections cannot become production S.8 authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 0 from the spec: Domain Skeleton And Subsystem Boundary Contract. Build the target topology as architectural homes, not as a report. Keep file-vs-directory shape flexible where the domain earns it, but do not soften ownership, lifecycle order, facade position, or authority direction.
phases.qa_focus: Check for meta-planning instead of skeleton implementation, vague crate ownership, broad lib.rs/mod.rs business logic, layout-indexes owning family execution, family crates depending on certification law, missing facade homes, missing responsibility-map tests, and fake compile-fail boundaries.

phases.title: Durable Artifact Family Inventory
acceptance: Every durable artifact family is declared with authority posture, lifecycle class, access lane, owning lower-crate boundary, rebuild/migration posture, and explicit non-authority projection classes.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 1 from the spec: Durable Artifact Family Inventory. Use the Phase 0 skeleton and place vocabulary in the selected artifact-family homes.
phases.qa_focus: Check for generic artifact bags, missing family owner, derived projection promoted to authority, broad scan loopholes, and inventory entries that cannot drive later admission.

phases.title: Artifact Authority And Lifecycle Classification
acceptance: Artifact authority and lifecycle classes are typed, denial-backed, and sufficient to distinguish authoritative, derived, diagnostic, terminal, certification, hot-path, maintenance, verifier, and readmission families.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 2 from the spec: Artifact Authority And Lifecycle Classification.
phases.qa_focus: Check for overloaded nouns, implicit authority, lifecycle states hidden in predicates, and certification/test labels acting as production classification.

phases.title: Authority Roles, Accuracy Classes, And Scope Partitioning
acceptance: Authority roles, derived accuracy classes, tenant/key-scope partitions, and non-claim security boundaries are typed and cannot be satisfied by identity-provider strings or copied metadata.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 3 from the spec: Authority Roles, Accuracy Classes, And Scope Partitioning.
phases.qa_focus: Check for tenant/key scope laundering, identity-provider claims as Store authority, projection/authority confusion, and missing cross-scope denial cases.

phases.title: Physical Key-Domain Law
acceptance: Physical key domains declare canonical encodings, comparators, prefix/range bounds, composite ordering, hash-collision behavior, and tenant/key partitioning with adversarial denials.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 4 from the spec: Physical Key-Domain Law.
phases.qa_focus: Check for string keys, implicit comparators, prefix/range ambiguity, tenant partition leaks, and hash collision denial gaps.

phases.title: Strategy Invariant Suites And Baseline B-Tree/LSM Algorithms
acceptance: Baseline B-tree and LSM strategy families have mechanically testable invariant suites for lookup, publication, mutation, integrity, recovery, separators, tombstones, and compaction ordering.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 5 from the spec: Strategy Invariant Suites And Baseline B-Tree/LSM Algorithms.
phases.qa_focus: Check for generic index vocabulary, fake B-tree/LSM claims, untested invariants, separator/tombstone/compaction gaps, and algorithms that cannot support later cost evidence.

phases.title: Materialization, Coverage, Freshness, And Absence Proofs
acceptance: Materialization state, coverage basis, freshness watermarks, coverage gaps, physical absence proofs, and range/prefix completeness witnesses are typed and deny stale or partial-index false absence.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 6 from the spec: Materialization, Coverage, Freshness, And Absence Proofs.
phases.qa_focus: Check for stale indexes accepted as exact, partial coverage as absence, hidden broad scans, weak freshness semantics, and copied coverage rows.

phases.title: Layout Strategy Vocabulary
acceptance: Layout strategy vocabulary is explicit per artifact family and preserves authority, derivation, materialization, rebuild, version, and access-shape posture.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 7 from the spec: Layout Strategy Vocabulary.
phases.qa_focus: Check for layout names without invariants, strategy as enum-only theater, and vocabulary that hides cost or ownership.

phases.title: Layout Strategy Admission Registry
acceptance: Strategies are admitted through typed requests, authority checks, invariant suites, capability outputs, and denial cases; no raw strategy fields can construct admitted layout.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 8 from the spec: Layout Strategy Admission Registry.
phases.qa_focus: Check for raw constructors, registry as mutable bag, family/strategy mismatch, missing invariant admission, and certification-owned registry law.

phases.title: Customization Boundary For Future Higher Layers
acceptance: Future customization has typed declaration/admission hooks without allowing app/user callbacks, industry guesses, or unproven plugins to become index authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 9 from the spec: Customization Boundary For Future Higher Layers.
phases.qa_focus: Check for callback authority, app-level semantic leakage, generic plugin bypasses, and guessed industry-specific index policy.

phases.title: Access Shape Contracts
acceptance: Point, range, prefix, scan, streaming, append, compaction, rebuild, verifier, repair, quarantine, and degraded exact scan access shapes have explicit contracts and denial cases.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 10 from the spec: Access Shape Contracts.
phases.qa_focus: Check for broad scans masquerading as bounded access, missing streaming/repair/verifier distinctions, and access-shape claims without counters.

phases.title: Deterministic Plan Selection And Pre-Execution Budget Admission
acceptance: Access alternatives lower through deterministic selection, plan fingerprints, cost estimates, admitted budgets, and planned counter envelopes before execution.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 11 from the spec: Deterministic Plan Selection And Pre-Execution Budget Admission.
phases.qa_focus: Check for nondeterministic selection, after-the-fact budgets, hidden fallbacks, missing plan fingerprint, and planned counters detached from execution.

phases.title: Access Lowering And Proof Progression
acceptance: Access lowering follows forge-proof progression from declaration/admission into lowered, ready, executed, denied, deferred, stale, rebind, or readmission outcomes without collapsing non-success cases.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 12 from the spec: Access Lowering And Proof Progression.
phases.qa_focus: Check for boolean success/failure collapse, stale as success, raw ready-plan constructors, and missing next-capability types.

phases.title: Rebuild Source And Derived Index Consistency
acceptance: Derived index rebuilds declare source authority, rebuild plan, parity witness, corruption behavior, and denial when derived data is treated as source truth.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 13 from the spec: Rebuild Source And Derived Index Consistency.
phases.qa_focus: Check for derived projection authority, self-comparison rebuild proof, missing parity source, and corrupted derived state masking authority corruption.

phases.title: Live Index Maintenance And Publication Protocols
acceptance: Live maintenance modes, mutation plans, publication protocols, lag witnesses, and maintenance failure outcomes are explicit for maintained derived layouts.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 14 from the spec: Live Index Maintenance And Publication Protocols.
phases.qa_focus: Check for mutation side effects without publication, lag hidden as current, missing cutover protocol, and maintenance failures converted into ordinary reads.

phases.title: Corruption, Quarantine, And Readmission Semantics
acceptance: Layout corruption, quarantine, readmission, authoritative-vs-derived corruption, terminal imports, and offline evidence have distinct outcomes and cannot become foreground authority without Store readmission.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 15 from the spec: Corruption, Quarantine, And Readmission Semantics.
phases.qa_focus: Check for corruption converted into empty result, offline verifier authority leakage, terminal serde authority, and missing readmission transitions.

phases.title: Versioning, Migration, And Rollback
acceptance: Layout versions, compatibility windows, migration plans, rollback plans, stale/rebind outcomes, and interruption behavior are typed and tested.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 16 from the spec: Versioning, Migration, And Rollback.
phases.qa_focus: Check for mixed-version ambiguity, rollback trusting derived state, migration without interruption proof, and stale layout accepted as exact.

phases.title: Amplification And Exact Counter Evidence
acceptance: Executed access produces exact access-path, read-amplification, write-amplification, page-touch, probe, and planned-versus-observed counter receipts.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 17 from the spec: Amplification And Exact Counter Evidence.
phases.qa_focus: Check for copied counters, weak counter strength, planned counters detached from execution, and Foundational reports used before Store execution.

phases.title: Bootstrap Catalog And Minimal Root Discovery
acceptance: Bootstrap catalog and minimal root discovery are tiny, fixed, versioned, checksummed, and incapable of answering ordinary access except through bootstrap-only admission.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 18 from the spec: Bootstrap Catalog And Minimal Root Discovery.
phases.qa_focus: Check for bootstrap catalog as general index, unchecked root discovery, missing version/checksum, and ordinary access through bootstrap-only paths.

phases.title: Page, Frame, Segment, And Extent Layout Families
acceptance: Page, frame, segment, and extent families consume S.8 grammar through their local layout_access homes and preserve physical-format byte authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 19 from the spec: Page, Frame, Segment, And Extent Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for layout law duplicated in physical-format, physical bytes delegated to layout-indexes, root/extent broad scans, and missing family counters.

phases.title: Root Manifest, Allocation, Free-Space, And Placement Layout Families
acceptance: Root manifest, allocation, free-space, and placement families have declared strategies, access shapes, counters, corruption behavior, and no implicit whole-store scan fallback.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 20 from the spec: Root Manifest, Allocation, Free-Space, And Placement Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for allocation/free-space scans hidden as lookup, stale root publication, placement residue as authority, and missing absence proof.

phases.title: WAL And Checkpoint Layout Families
acceptance: WAL and checkpoint families declare append, tail, checkpoint, replay, and recovery access paths while keeping WAL authority local.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 21 from the spec: WAL And Checkpoint Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for backend residue authority, checkpoint/WAL mixed truth, unbounded tail scans, and layout-indexes owning WAL semantics.

phases.title: Recovery, Replay, And Crash-Boundary Index Families
acceptance: Recovery, replay, crash-boundary, checkpoint-cutover, and readmission layout families preserve recovery physics and deny ambiguous residue or derived rollback authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 22 from the spec: Recovery, Replay, And Crash-Boundary Index Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for crash-state collapse, residue guessing, replay self-comparison, and missing rebind/readmission states.

phases.title: Snapshot, Branch, And Continuation Layout Families
acceptance: Snapshot, branch, continuation, and stable-basis families declare access paths without stealing semantic MVCC/branch truth from higher layers.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 23 from the spec: Snapshot, Branch, And Continuation Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for semantic truth leakage, branch identity as physical authority, snapshot broad scans, and stale continuation access.

phases.title: Blob Object, Chunk-Tree, And Streaming Layout Families
acceptance: Blob object, chunk-tree, and streaming families consume S.8 grammar while preserving S.7 blob lifecycle authority, constant-memory access, and chunk-tree invariants.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 24 from the spec: Blob Object, Chunk-Tree, And Streaming Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for whole-blob materialization, chunk-tree root as generic index, streaming hidden buffers, and blob authority moved into layout-indexes.

phases.title: Blob Dedupe, Reachability, Retention, Reclaim, And Compaction Layout Families
acceptance: Blob dedupe, reachability, retention, reclaim, and compaction families declare access strategies, rebuild/parity, corruption, and scope-safe absence behavior.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 25 from the spec: Blob Dedupe, Reachability, Retention, Reclaim, And Compaction Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for digest-only dedupe, false reclaim absence, retention hold bypass, compaction identity drift, and cross-scope leaks.

phases.title: Maintenance, Tiering, And I/O Scheduler Layout Families
acceptance: Maintenance, tiering, recall, foreground/background pacing, and I/O scheduler layout families declare access budgets, interference posture, and exact counters.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 26 from the spec: Maintenance, Tiering, And I/O Scheduler Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for scheduler as layout authority, maintenance scans as cheap access, tier recall stale handles, and missing foreground-interference evidence.

phases.title: Security And Custody Lookup Layout Families
acceptance: Security, custody, key-scope, tenant-scope, authenticity, and repair blast-radius lookup families use S.5.1 posture and deny identity-provider strings as Store authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 27 from the spec: Security And Custody Lookup Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for JWT/org/KMS/IAM/operator identity laundering, custody as deployment folklore, and scope partitions missing from key domains.

phases.title: Export, Import, Capsule, And Offline Verifier Layout Families
acceptance: Export, import, capsule, backup/restore, and offline verifier layout evidence remains terminal until readmitted and cannot become foreground authority directly.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 28 from the spec: Export, Import, Capsule, And Offline Verifier Layout Families.
phases.qa_focus: Check for terminal projection re-entry, offline verifier as authority, backup after key rotation without readmission, and imported JSON/serde authority.

phases.title: Legacy Surface Disposition And Dedicated Workspace Boundary
acceptance: Every old access-path surface receives explicit disposition and cannot bypass declaration, admission, selection, budget, lowering, readiness, execution, or readmission.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 29 from the spec: Legacy Surface Disposition And Dedicated Workspace Boundary.
phases.qa_focus: Check for ambiguous legacy helpers, fallback classes as production paths, old topology precedent, and deep imports bypassing S.8 facades.

phases.title: Public Facades And Directory Shape
acceptance: Public imports reveal lifecycle order and authority posture rather than a flat ontology; code-quality QA clears concrete topology findings.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 30 from the spec: Public Facades And Directory Shape.
phases.qa_focus: Check for broad lib.rs dumps, mod.rs business logic, helper bins, god functions, public raw constructors, and facades that hide lifecycle order.

phases.title: Certification Harness Vocabulary And Scenario Skeleton
acceptance: The harness can describe layout law through scenarios, actors, faults, observers, oracles, transcripts, coverage, shortcut denials, and closeout evidence without becoming production law.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 31 from the spec: Certification Harness Vocabulary And Scenario Skeleton.
phases.qa_focus: Check for harness constructors minting authority, scenario-only success, certification-owned law, weak oracles, and missing shortcut denial taxonomy.

phases.title: Compile-Fail Authority And Facade Proofs
acceptance: Compile-fail proofs show external crates cannot raw-construct admitted layouts, ready access, executed counter receipts, readmitted witnesses, or certification/test fixture authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 32 from the spec: Compile-Fail Authority And Facade Proofs.
phases.qa_focus: Check for runtime-only denial wrappers, public fields, deep-import bypass, copied receipt construction, and missing facade misuse proofs.

phases.title: Runtime Simulation And Integration Certification
acceptance: Runtime simulations cover core physical, recovery, blob, maintenance/I/O, security/custody/export families with adversarial success, denial, corruption, rebuild, readmission, and cost evidence.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 33 from the spec: Runtime Simulation And Integration Certification.
phases.qa_focus: Check for representative-only happy paths, missing production actors, same-run self-comparison, weak counters, and simulations that bypass production facades.

phases.title: Transition Fact Authority
phases.owner: `forge-store-layout-indexes` owner outcome families and lower owner transition emitters
acceptance: Production layout outcomes, not S.9 handoff tables, are the source of sealed S.8 transition facts, and S.9 inventory is aggregation-only.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 34 from the spec: Transition Fact Authority. Do not restart the milestone or revisit earlier phases. Continue from the current dirty S.8 workspace and narrow the existing Phase 34 repair to transition-fact authority only.
phases.qa_focus: Check for parallel static S.9 contract tables, hand-authored transition arrays acting as authority, owner outcomes that do not expose sealed transition facts, compaction projection tables, and tests that prove table consistency instead of production equivalence.

phases.title: WAL And Manifest Membership Authority
phases.owner: `forge-store-wal` with certification consuming owner evidence only
acceptance: Baseline LSM membership, freshness, retirement, and compaction publication derive from WAL/manifest authority; journals are derived caches and cannot forge membership.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 35 from the spec: WAL And Manifest Membership Authority. Consume the Phase 34 transition-fact authority; do not widen back into S.9 handoff or closeout work.
phases.qa_focus: Check for caller-authored WAL membership, arbitrary manifest paths, digest-only retirement, certification-authored membership, journal rows promoted to authority, missing store/scope/checkpoint/coverage binding, and missing valid-forgery hostile tests.

phases.title: Layout Hazard Inventory And S.9 Handoff Assembly
acceptance: S.8 hazards map to real compile-fail, runtime, simulation, or formal-model sources, and S.9 receives explicit layout/access state machines from owner evidence rather than generic summaries.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 36 from the spec: Layout Hazard Inventory And S.9 Handoff Assembly. This phase assembles the handoff after Phases 34 and 35 supply real owner sources.
phases.qa_focus: Check for generic S.9 summaries, copied counters, copied receipts, certification fixture outputs, table-only state-machine rows, vague residual risk, and hazard rows without owner-source coverage.

phases.title: Hostile Certification Boundary Proof
acceptance: Certification consumes owner evidence as courtroom material and cannot mint transition facts, WAL membership, retirement authority, or S.9 readiness.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 37 from the spec: Hostile Certification Boundary Proof. Prove the shortcuts found during the old overloaded Phase 34 loop are mechanically denied.
phases.qa_focus: Check for certification overreach, private-constructor test shortcuts, transition substitution, static contract substitution, forged WAL rows, equal-digest cross-scope retirement, same-root cross-store redirection, manifest disagreement, duplicate replay, ordering disagreement, and weak compile-fail coverage.

phases.title: Workspace-Wide Closeout And S.9 Handoff
acceptance: S.8 closeout proves every admitted durable artifact family has declared strategy, key-domain law, access shape, authority posture, counters, corruption/rebuild behavior, trust-boundary behavior, legacy disposition, and S.9 handoff evidence.
phases.instructions: Implement S.8 Phase 38 from the spec: Workspace-Wide Closeout And S.9 Handoff. Close only after Phases 34-37 are complete.
phases.qa_focus: Check for hidden generic layout fallback, missing family closeout, weak counter evidence, unverified B-tree/LSM claims, skeleton drift, and closeout that omits runtime or compile-fail proof.
